# Preserve unrelated vendor name overlaps

The published4.0.0 actual-machine plan stopped before native manager actions: independent finance/design plugins share local helper names such as meeting-prep/user-context. The native observer incorrectly rejected duplicates entirely outside the managed set. Codex qualifies plugin skill names; the updater must also preserve pre-existing unrelated packages without treating their overlaps as authority to modify them.

Two fresh real-isolated Codex/Pi tests reproduce the failure before the change. The correction deduplicates only the comparison set of unrelated names; the full registrations and payloads remain bound by unrelatedHash. Managed-to-managed and managed-to-vendor conflicts still fail closed. The tests perform actual isolated withdrawal/exposure, assert unchanged unrelated config/payload hashes, and then introduce a managed collision to verify rejection. All19native adapter tests pass afterward. Original failure logs remain.

This is a forward patch release, not a retag or rollback of4.0.0. Actual installed-package migration has not executed. A read-only diagnostic using the repaired observer against the published checkout is separate from release qualification and grants no mutation authority.

A read-only live preview then found schema1 source hashes were checkout-mode dependent: the same catalog bytes were0600 in the stable checkout and0664 in the isolated worktree; package directories were0700/0775. No permission was changed. Acceptance schema2 normalizes source digest modes to Git's regular/executable semantics while retaining every path/kind/byte digest. The old schema stays supported with its original strict semantics. All local transaction snapshots remain unchanged and still detect permission changes after planning. Two regression tests verify permission portability and rejection of executable changes, added paths, changed bytes and unknown formats; seven acceptance tests pass. Final obligations also bind the ten migration/acceptance implementation files, not only skill/catalog sources.
